title: What Is Yours to Answer For? / 职责与承担
scope: Three reader essays from one later special study. Complete Simplified and Traditional Chinese plus independent English rewrites. Added as a distinct companion beside the existing seven Rights Theory essays, not as a claim that the new work has eight-language editions.
method: Lead read the full 26,993-character Chinese paper, authored and self-edited the three Chinese essays and independent English versions, read all three generated Traditional Chinese bodies and corrected contextual forms. No subagents or translation service used for this batch.

coverage.sections: Introduction; I F36–38; II F40–41, with source-tracing and registration boundaries
coverage.focus: Where a demand comes from; functioning rights relations versus bare force; registration need not be formal paperwork, voluntary choice or approval; person, function and appointment; separate demands in one appointment; demand versus performance, including omission. Disappointment alone proves no applicable demand.

Two independently grounded chains, no universal quid pro quo; institutional attribution versus actual execution and independently grounded personal accountability; liability is exposure to positional change, can be empty and need not involve fault; classification gives no legitimacy; minimum standing is not full protection; obstruction decides neither fault nor all consequences; no automatic quantitative power-accountability law.

coverage.sections: IV F47–52; VI F57–58; VII F59–61; VIII open questions
coverage.focus: Generation, completion, exit and failure are different; actual exit ends the ongoing load grounded in that registration, not history or independently continuing sources; carrier change need not change registration; scope-sensitive withdrawal; inward undertaking may coexist without freezing its concrete content; succession and children require item-by-item tracing, not an automatic transfer or unchallengeable threshold.

boundaries: The office, employment and child cases are invented illustrations, not documented contracts or legal holdings. No instructions about an actual labor dispute, remedies, post-employment confidentiality or minors' statutory obligations are issued.

The paper stipulates technical senses for accountability, liability and inward duty. The essays distinguish these from ordinary and legal meanings and do not claim every tradition's duty theory shares one model.
Classifying a demand neither endorses it nor provides practical protection. Actual coercion is not removed by changing its name; lack of accountability does not imply that coercion must remain.

Registration's occurrence and a demand's legitimacy are separate, but bare force is not promoted into accountability. Operative rights, source, content and actual relation remain necessary; psychological endorsement is not a substitute.

Ending a registration terminates the ongoing load dependent on it, including continuing demands in that same registration. Historical acts and nonperformance persist; other current grounds must be checked separately. No unlimited residual moral debt is invented, and no blanket exemption is inferred.

A child's developing ability does not distribute all accountability; actual actor and bearer are distinct. Unmet matters can remain identified without an invented successor; not yet identifying a bearer is not proving none exists.
Clear revisable age rules and procedures are not ruled out wholesale; the target is a rigid, cross-context, unchallengeable substitute for item-by-item judgment.
